title: How to tailor a resume to a job description | SearchBreaker
description: A step-by-step method for tailoring a resume to a job description using only your real experience, with a checklist and common mistakes to avoid.

breadcrumbs.label: How to tailor a resume to a job description

blocks.headline: How to tailor a resume to a job description
blocks.answer: Match each requirement in the job description to real evidence from your experience, then reorder and reword your resume so that evidence is easy to find.

blocks.text: Recruiters and applicant tracking systems both compare your resume with the job description. A tailored resume makes the overlap easy to see. It needs no new experience, only clearer wording and ordering of what you already did.
Tailor your resume in five steps

steps.title: List the job’s requirements
steps.text: Copy the must-have and nice-to-have items into two lists. Skip generic phrases like “team player”.

steps.title: Match each requirement to evidence
steps.text: For each item, find a role, project or result that shows it. Mark gaps honestly.

steps.title: Reorder, then reword
steps.text: Move the most relevant roles and bullets up. Use the job’s terms where they describe the same work.

steps.title: Cut what does not support this job
steps.text: Shorten or remove bullets that do not relate to the requirements.

steps.title: Check every claim
steps.text: Read each line and confirm you can explain it in an interview.

blocks.title: Never add experience you do not have
blocks.text: Using the job’s wording is fine when it describes real work. Adding skills or results you cannot back up can end an interview process.

blocks.caption: When to tailor and when to rewrite
rows: Small edits to wording and order
Higher: new wording can drift from facts
Roles similar to your recent work

blocks.text: Repeat a term only where it describes something you did. A list of keywords without context rarely helps, and recruiters notice it.

items: Use the job’s exact term once, where it fits a real bullet.
Keep your own wording elsewhere so the resume still reads naturally.
Do not hide keywords in white text or tiny fonts.

blocks.title: Keep a master list of facts
blocks.text: Write down every role, result and skill once. Tailoring then becomes selecting and rewording, not remembering.

items: Tailoring changes wording and order, not facts.
Map each requirement to real evidence before you edit.
Use the job’s terms only where they describe your actual work.
Check every line before you send.

blocks.title: Tailor each resume from verified facts
blocks.text: SearchBreaker maps job requirements to the experience you confirmed and proposes edits you approve one by one.

faqs.a: Tailor for every role you actively want. For very similar roles, small changes to the summary and the order of bullets are often enough.

faqs.q: Is it okay to copy phrases from the job description?
faqs.a: Yes, where the phrase describes work you actually did. Copying requirements you do not meet misleads the reader.

faqs.q: Does tailoring help with applicant tracking systems?
faqs.a: Clear headings, plain text and the job’s own terms make a resume easier to parse. No method guarantees how a specific system will read it.
